Asthma - Acute
“All that wheezes is not asthma”
Important Differential Diagnosis
Assess Clinical Severity
Look at vital signs; level of consciousness; work of breathing
Do not need lab tests to assess severity.
START TREATMENT ASAP – do not delay life-saving therapy
Assess response to treatment
Reassess patient (including vital signs) after initial treatment is instituted

Asthma - Acute 
Other Things To Do
 
1. Consider the trigger (commonly viral infection) 
2. Monitor and replace IV fluids (increased 
insensible losses and increased vascular tone-may 
precipitously drop BP during intubation if not 
given fluid bolus) 
3. Maintain O2 Saturation 94-98% 
4. Monitor and replace K+ (β2 agonist and steroids will 
drop K+) 
5. Chest X-Ray (if patient hypoxic (O2 Sats <92%) on 
room air) 
Criteria for Admission
 
1. Poor response to therapy 
2. Hypoxia on room air (O2 Sats <92%) 
3. High risk features present 
High Risk Features for Death
 
1. Previous near fatal exacerbation/ intubation/ ICU 
admission 
2. Use of >2 canisters of short-acting β2 agonist in last 
month 
3. Recent course of steroids 
4. Admission or ED visit in last month 
o >2 admissions in last year 
o >3 ED visits in last year 
5. Illicit drug use 
6. Psychiatric history 
7. Cardiac and/or lung disease as co-morbidities 
 
Criteria for Discharge from the ED
 
1. Pulse <110bpm, RR <25bpm, O2 Saturation >92% on 
room air 
2. Patient’s improvement and response to therapy is 
sustained for 1 hour after last nebulisation. 
3. Peak flow >75% of patient’s best/ predicted 
4. Improvement in patient’s subjective symptoms 
(poorest sign for safe discharge). 
If Intubated 
Ventilator Settings 
MODE                     SIMV 
TV                            6-8 mℓ/kg 
I:E                            1:3 
RR                           10-12 bpm (child 20bpm) 
ALARM                   Maximum 
 
If Deterioration After Intubation Consider:
1. Displacement of ET tube if intubated 
2. Obstruction of ET tube/ mucous plug 
3. Pneumothorax/ pneumomediastinum 
4. Equipment failure/ disconnection 
5. Suctioning required/ stomach overdistension 
 
Discharge Plan 
1. Re-start maintenance medication and check MDI administration technique 
o β2 agonist MDI-salbutamol (asthavent®)/ fenoterol (berotec®) QID PRN 
o Inhaled steroid-budesonide (budeflam®) 400μg BD 
2. Supplemental short-course steroids 
Oral prednisone 0.5mg/kg po daily x 1/52 (if compliance expected to be good) 
OR 
Dexamethasone (Decadron®) 10mg IM STAT 
(2.5mℓ of 4mg/mℓ vials) 
3. Follow-up at local clinic/ polyclinic with referral letter
